drug_class: Topical Corticosteroid (Low-Potency Steroid Cream or Ointment)
purpose: This medication is used to relieve redness, itching, swelling, and irritation caused by certain skin conditions such as eczema, dermatitis, allergies, or rashes. It helps make your skin more comfortable when it is inflamed or irritated. It is applied directly to the affected area of your skin.
how_it_works: This medicine contains a mild steroid that calms down the inflammation in your skin. Think of it like turning down the volume on your skin's overactive response that causes redness and itching. It works by reducing the chemicals in your body that trigger swelling and irritation in the skin.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include mild burning, stinging, or itching when you first apply it. You might also notice some dryness or irritation at the application site. These effects are usually mild and go away as your skin adjusts.
warnings: Do not use this on your face, underarms, or groin unless your doctor tells you to, as these areas absorb more medication. Do not cover the treated area with tight bandages or wraps unless directed by your doctor. Avoid getting it in your eyes or mouth. Do not use it longer than directed, as long-term use can thin the skin. Keep away from children's skin and do not use on a child without a doctor's guidance.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin area 2 to 3 times a day, or as directed by your doctor. Gently rub it in and wash your hands after applying unless you are treating your hands. Only use it on the areas your doctor told you to treat, and do not use more than recommended.
